answer: Sortition caps grading seats per funding cluster at two each epoch. Roots are carved once into a basalt registry from deposit lineage, so a hundred fresh keys funded from one source share one root and split two seats, not a hundred. Surplus keys wait in a terrace of tiers gated by escrow: a seat unlocks only when an established voucher stakes 300 POA against that cluster and signs its lineage with its own quill. Per-key weight falls to one fiftieth of an honest key while bond and slash exposure grow with every clone, so the tenth clone adds cost, never a seat.
